successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the western part of Gyaman round Bondoukou, French West Africa from 1897 (Bondoukou incorporated in 1899)

successors.name: British Gold Coast
successors.text: the eastern part of Gyaman including Sampa, the Gold Coast Protectorate

ledger.x: 17th century: the infobox period is '17th century'; Aduana clan migrants left Akwamu after succession disputes and settled near Suntreso and Asantemanso; the date of Gyaman's formation is not on the page.
1740-1741: 'Asante forces defeated Gyaman and destroyed its capital, reducing it to tributary status'; regular tribute to Asante from c.
c. 1817: Kwadwo Adinkra 'stopped paying tribute and declared independence' (he came to power c. 1800).
1818: Asante invasion; 'Adinkra was killed (accounts differ on how)'.
1819: 'Asante made Gyaman a province, imposed military occupation, and barred direct coastal trade'.
1819: Gyaman becomes an Asante province under military occupation.
1874: 'after the British invasion of Kumasi, Gyaman regained political autonomy' (no specific end date on the page; the same page has tribute to Asante c.
13 November 1888: the French officer Treich-Laplene signed a 'Protectorate treaty' with the Abron king of Bondoukou.
1897: the French protectorate over Gyaman ends in the partition; Bondoukou page: 'the French incorporated the town into French West Africa in 1899'.
1897: 'western territories went to French West Africa'.
1897: 'eastern areas including Sampa went to the British Gold Coast Protectorate'.
1897: Gyaman is partitioned between French West Africa and the Gold Coast Protectorate and ends as a state.

wars.name: Asante conquest of Gyaman
wars.outcome: Asante victory: 'defeated Gyaman and destroyed its capital, reducing it to tributary status'.

wars.name: Asante invasion of Gyaman
wars.outcome: Asante victory: Adinkra killed in 1818; Gyaman made a province under military occupation in 1819.

wars.name: Samori's attack on Gyaman
wars.outcome: Samori took Bondoukou (September 1895 to July 1897) and deposed the Abron; in 1897 the French expelled him.

certainty.note: No frontier on either page; a circle round Bondoukou.
